title: Corporate Device Health Check Guide
problem: Employee reports that the corporate device is slow, unstable, or not functioning normally.
prerequisites: Power adapter is connected if using a laptop.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Restart the Device
troubleshooting_steps.instruction: Restart the computer and verify whether performance improves.
troubleshooting_steps.caption: Restart Windows

troubleshooting_steps.title: Check CPU and Memory Usage
troubleshooting_steps.instruction: Open Task Manager and review CPU, Memory and Disk utilization.
troubleshooting_steps.caption: Task Manager

troubleshooting_steps.title: Check Disk Space
troubleshooting_steps.instruction: Ensure the system drive has at least 15–20% free space.
troubleshooting_steps.caption: Disk Space

troubleshooting_steps.title: Run Device Health Scan
troubleshooting_steps.instruction: Run the corporate device health diagnostic or Device Agent scan.
troubleshooting_steps.caption: Device Health Scan

troubleshooting_steps.title: Verify Performance
troubleshooting_steps.instruction: Open common business applications and confirm that the system responds normally.
troubleshooting_steps.caption: Performance Verification

common_errors.resolution: Identify the consuming process in Task Manager and close unnecessary applications.
Remove unnecessary files or contact IT for storage assistance.
Restart the device and perform a health scan.

escalation.condition: Escalate if performance remains poor after troubleshooting or hardware diagnostics report failures.

faq.question: Why is my laptop suddenly slow?
faq.answer: High CPU, insufficient memory, low disk space, or background applications are common causes.

faq.question: Should I restart my computer first?
faq.answer: Yes. Restarting often resolves temporary performance issues.
